reading.body:
Microsoft's West Des Moines campus spans Polk, Dallas, and Warren counties and is one of three Iowa facilities with published capacity data, though Microsoft does not disclose megawatt figures or footprint for individual campuses. The operator has reported $1.5 to $2 billion invested in the West Des Moines site with a sixth data center, codenamed Ruthenium, in planning stages. Exact power consumption and building-level specifications remain unpublished by policy.

This campus ranks third among Iowa's 52 mapped facilities by published megawatt capacity, behind two other undisclosed sites, in a state with only 18 MW of published AI infrastructure capacity across all operators. The absence of disclosed capacity figures means the campus's significance to AI scaling cannot be assessed from power metrics alone.

Microsoft's disclosure policy treats all individual campus specifications as proprietary, making this facility's contribution to US AI compute capacity readable only through regional investment announcements and planning records rather than engineering specifications. The reported scale of investment and planned expansion suggest material importance to the company's cloud infrastructure, but no technical fact confirms the volume of compute deployed or its trajectory.
